finding: The selected reference specs/request-consistency.md#requirements is not provided in the request inputs, so its requirement cannot be compared with the issue scope. Promotion Runtime depends on a request-bound artifact path and an immutable request identity (requestId and inputPath binding), and no provided input defines that request identity or its binding rules. The request-binding acceptance check cannot be judged from the request.

The conditional export retention requirement names docs/adr/0005-external-policy.md#decision as the authoritative source for a 30-day retention duration for a generated-artifact export. ADR 0005 states that it is the authoritative source only for promotion artifact retention. No provided input gives an authoritative source for the duration of a reader-link target export that is not a promotion artifact, so that obligation has no applicable authority in the request.

Whether the conditional export retention requirement applies depends on whether the new reader-index target docs/reference/validation-report.md is a generated artifact or a manually maintained document. The reader index requirement names the target, and the architecture excerpt states only that the target already exists. No provided input states its kind, so the applicability of the selected conditional retention obligation cannot be established from the request.

The selected reference specs/image-cache.md#preview-cleanup defines a 24-hour cleanup of documentation-renderer image previews. The issue's What to build section lists the Validation Report, Result Summary, invalid-input diagnostic wording, indexed cache lookup, single-scan parser strategy, protected access review, promotion, recovery, runtime migration and Reader Index Update, and states that listing a behavior is what defines delivery. Preview cleanup is not among them, so this selected requirement is outside the delivery and cannot expand or authorize the implementation scope.

The runtime migration requirement states that the promote(inputPath) successful result is exactly {status: 'succeeded', artifactId, trackedStateId}. The selected Result Summary requirement states that the same successful result must include a string summary field. The two selected requirements give incompatible exact successful result contracts for the same caller-visible result, so an implementation and its public lifecycle tests cannot know which shape is required.

The runtime migration requirement states that an expected filesystem failure is exactly {recovered: false, failureCode, priorTrackedState, baselineStatus}, which omits operation. The same requirement cites Promotion Runtime for failure value semantics, and Promotion Runtime defines the expected filesystem failure as {recovered: false, failureCode, operation, priorTrackedState, baselineStatus}. The two exact field sets conflict, so the caller-visible result for an expected filesystem failure is not determined.

The selected Authorization Behavior requirement says that an allowed operation reads the artifact, but it does not identify the artifact source. It also sends invalid policy, invalid facts and Artifact Reader failure results to the Other Results contract of the Interfaces section. The issue selects only the Requirements heading of this spec, so the read source and those failure results are not defined in the selected scope and the requirement cannot be implemented or verified from its own text.

The selected Complete Operation Contract requirement says that invalid recoverPromotion input is returned according to the Interfaces Invalid Input Diagnostic. The selected Requirements do not define that diagnostic's failureCode, path or details message, and the issue selects only the Requirements heading, which excludes the Interfaces section that defines it. The invalid-input result therefore cannot be implemented or verified from the selected requirement.

The selected Promotion Behavior requirement says that expected filesystem failures and rollback failures return the Interfaces structured diagnostic, but the selected Requirements do not define their failure result shape, operation or failure codes. Those details are only in the unselected Interfaces section, so the selected requirement does not itself define the caller-visible failure results it is meant to deliver.

The retention requirement says that a successful tracked artifact is kept for 30 days and that removal after expiry is not part of the promote operation. No selected requirement and no provided input assigns removal after the 30-day period to any owner, and no selected requirement defines what persistence must do with the applied retention value. This is an unresolved persistent-state decision: the 30-day retention cannot be verified as implemented, and no responsible module is identified for its expiry.

The Result Summary requirement adds a human-readable summary sentence to the canonical successful promote result. The output contract states that the canonical caller result is structured JSON and that a reader presentation does not change the canonical result, and the user context states the same separation. The selected requirement changes the canonical result with a display sentence that restates artifactId and trackedStateId, which conflicts with the provided current output contract.
